title: Worksheet 6: Pixels and Digital Images
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: Every image displayed on a computer screen, from a simple icon to a detailed photograph, is made up of thousands or millions of tiny colored squares called pixels. The word "pixel" is short for "picture element." Each pixel displays a single solid color, and when many pixels are placed close together in a grid, they blend together to form a complete image, similar to how tiny tiles form a mosaic picture. The number of pixels in an image is called its "resolution." An image with more pixels, called a "higher resolution" image, can show finer detail, while an image with fewer pixels, called a "lower resolution" image, looks blocky or blurry when enlarged, because each individual pixel becomes more visible. Each pixel's color is typically created by mixing different amounts of red, green, and blue light, a system known as RGB, since combining these three colors in different amounts can produce millions of different colors.
